The papersThe code

CoLP, dug back up.

CoLP mapped where proteins sit in normal brain and in glioma, and which ones move. Its server is gone and its code was never released. We rebuilt it from the paper and its 2008 method paper, reran it on the archived data, and checked 35 results on 2026-11-18: 7 agree, 8 partly agree, 11 differ and 9 were not attempted.

The possibility formula, applied as printed, puts the median possibility at 0.39, so 'possibility 0.40' cannot also mean P < 0.005 as the paper says. Calling locations by P < 0.005 instead gives under half the paper's locations (13,362 against 29,999) and just over half its proteins (5,091 against 9,543). The calibration (Suppl. Fig. S5) is in the unavailable supplement.

The paper's own numbers against each otherAgrees
Random and permuted-expression controls (Suppl. Figs S12, S13, S35)Not attemptedThe supplementary figures with the numbers, and the permutation scheme, are in the Genome Research supplement, which could not be fetched; our maps do not reproduce the 15 validated mislocations to begin with.
Supplemental Tables S1 and S2 (all predictions, 157 mislocations)Not attemptedThe tables are on genome.cshlp.org only, behind a Cloudflare challenge; the CoLP server that also served them is gone.
Python package condloc and its tutorialAgrees

The static part of the method holds: interacting proteins that are co-expressed share a location most often, and network features predict GO locations about as well as the paper says. The condition-specific part does not come back: our maps move few proteins between normal brain and glioma, and none of the 15 validated mislocations. The causes are the settings the unavailable supplement holds (the possibility calibration and the mislocation test) and a rebuilt gold standard and network.

What came back

Table 1D
The five GEO series give 82, 23 and 134 samples, as published.
Fig. 2A
Interacting pairs with correlated expression share a location 80% of the time, 0.08 more than pairs with opposed expression (paper 0.1).
Fig. 2D
Single-protein features average an AUC of 0.63, as published.
Fig. 2B
The four feature configurations rank as in the paper, 0.03 to 0.08 lower.
Location maps
RET at the plasma membrane and SMAD4 in the nucleus in all three conditions, as published.
Package
condloc, the method as a Python package with a tutorial.

What stayed buried

  • The supplement (Tables S1 and S2, the calibration and the mislocation test) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge.
  • BIND is gone and DIP needs a login; the network is rebuilt from the sources still online.
  • The gold standard is rebuilt from GO in 2007 (4,597 proteins against Lee et al. 2008's 4,570); 4,269 of them still map to UniProt.
  • The wet-lab panels cannot be regenerated.

The static part of the method holds: interacting proteins that are co-expressed share a location most often, and network features predict GO locations about as well as the paper says. The condition-specific part does not come back: our maps move few proteins between normal brain and glioma, and none of the 15 validated mislocations. The causes are the settings the unavailable supplement holds (the possibility calibration and the mislocation test) and a rebuilt gold standard and network.

What we matched

What we put next to the paper, and how.

Gold standard
GO 2007-01-01, every evidence code but IEA, 13 locations.
Network
HPRD and Reactome (2011), Rual, Stelzl and Ewing (BioGRID 2011), Ramani 2005: 84,309 links between 10,351 proteins.
Expression
GSE5281 and GSE5390 (normal), GSE3185 and GSE9885 (low grade), GSE3185, GSE9885 and GSE4271 (high grade).
Classifier
DC-kNN with k = 5 and 29 feature sets, leave-two-out by halves.
Maps
Coherence-weighted network features per condition, degrees of possibility, P < 0.005 calls.

We dug CoLP back up on 2026-11-18. Its static half came back; its mislocations did not.
